sections.h2: How big is Gwinnett County and which cities does it hold?
sections.html:
Gwinnett County is a core county of metro Atlanta, about nine miles northeast of the Atlanta city limits, with Lawrenceville as the seat and Peachtree Corners as the largest city. It was created by the General Assembly on December 15, 1818, and named for Button Gwinnett, a signer of the Declaration of Independence (Wikipedia).

The county spans 437 square miles, 430 of them land, in the upper Piedmont along the Eastern Continental Divide. Lake Lanier touches its far north, and a slice of the Chattahoochee River National Recreation Area runs along the northwest. Its northeastern corner was cut away in 1914 to help form Barrow County. Forsyth, Hall, Jackson, Barrow, Walton, Rockdale, DeKalb and Fulton counties share its borders.

Fifteen cities sit wholly or partly inside the line: Auburn, Berkeley Lake, Buford, Dacula, Duluth, Grayson, Lawrenceville, Lilburn, Loganville, Mulberry, Norcross, Peachtree Corners, Snellville, Sugar Hill and Suwanee. Braselton and Rest Haven are towns, and Mountain Park is a census-designated place. Some of these straddle a county line, so confirm on the parcel record which tax commissioner bills you.

sections.h2: What do roads, schools and employers mean for a Gwinnett seller?
sections.html:
Interstate 85 and Interstate 985 are the main freeways, with US 23, US 29, US 78 and State Routes 8, 13 and 20 feeding them. The county runs Gwinnett County Airport, and Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International is the nearest major airport. The Census Bureau puts the average trip to work at 32.8 minutes, a figure worth remembering when you describe the location to buyers.

Gwinnett County Public Schools is the largest district in Georgia, with 143 schools: 21 high schools, 29 middle schools, 80 elementary schools and 13 specialty schools. Residents inside the Buford city limits are served by Buford City School District instead. Georgia Gwinnett College and Gwinnett Technical College are both in Lawrenceville.

Employers listed by Wikipedia include AGCO in Duluth, Comcast's Southeast headquarters and ASHRAE in Peachtree Corners, Canon's regional office in Norcross, and Primerica and Waffle House near Duluth and Norcross. The school district and city named on your bill depend on where the parcel sits, so note both when you describe the property.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Gwinnett County?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 957,062 people, second only to Fulton among Georgia's counties. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 1,018,099, a rise of 6.3% over the estimates base, and the county has 356,091 housing units. About 28.4% of residents were born abroad.

sections.h2: Who do I call about Gwinnett County property tax?
sections.html:
The county splits the job among several offices, and the tax commissioner's brochure lists each one. The commissioner bills, collects and disburses tax and is not involved in setting the amount. Values come from the Board of Assessors, millage rates from the commissioners, the school board and each city.

  • Property tax (tax commissioner): 770-822-8800, tax@gwinnettcounty.com, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday.
  • Board of Assessors, real property: 770-822-7200; personal property: 770-822-7220. Values and appeals go through Gwinnett-Assessor.com.
  • Board of Commissioners, county millage rates and fees: 770-822-7000.
  • Board of Education, school millage: 678-301-6200.
  • Clerk of Court, deeds and liens: 770-822-8100.

The commissioner's brochure page is the best single reference, and mail payments go to P.O. Box 372, Lawrenceville, GA 30046.

sections.h2: What is the Gwinnett County property tax calendar?
sections.html:
Gwinnett County gives its dates as typical ones that can change, so a bill in your hand beats any chart. The brochure lays out this sequence:

  • January: mobile home bills are mailed, and they are due April 1.
  • April 1: personal property returns for tangible business assets, aircraft and watercraft are due to the Board of Assessors.
  • May and June: the Annual Notice of Assessment is mailed, and an appeal must be filed within 45 days of the notice date.
  • July and August: taxing authorities set millage rates in advertised public sessions.
  • August or September: real and personal property bills are mailed and posted online.
  • October or November: bills are due.

The county printed November 15, 2025 as the previous due date and listed the 2026 date as to be determined, a date that the Board of Commissioners may change yearly. Check your own bill for the date that applies. Personal property worth more than $20,000 combined is taxable, and a late or unreported return may draw a 10% penalty. A delinquent mobile home bill carries 10% plus 1% interest per month after June 1.

sections.h2: How do I pay a Gwinnett County property tax bill?
sections.html:
Payment by check online is free, while credit and debit card payments online carry a convenience fee. You can also use the 24-hour drop boxes at all five tag offices, mail a check to the Lawrenceville post office box, or pay in person at any tax commissioner office during business hours. Cash is accepted in person only, and the county asks that no cash be sent by mail.

Some cities bill property tax on their own rather than through the county. The commissioner collects mobile home, heavy-duty equipment and timber tax in every Gwinnett city, but for real property in a city that bills independently, contact that city's tax department.

sections.h2: Which exemptions apply in Gwinnett County?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption lowers the tax on a primary residence, and one application covers every exemption the county offers. Applications are taken year-round by mail, in person or online, and the owner must occupy the home as a legal primary residence on January 1. Once granted, an exemption continues until ownership or eligibility changes. If you mail it, the county recommends certified mail.

Gwinnett also has the Value Offset Exemption, a local measure that freezes a property's assessed value at its base-year value for the county government portion of the bill. School and city taxes are not covered. It is applied automatically when a homestead exemption is granted, and it covers the house and up to five acres of land. The Board of Assessors separately reviews conservation use, agricultural, historic and Brownfield preferential assessments and tax-exempt status for property such as places of worship.

sections.h2: What happens to Gwinnett County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
The January 1 owner is legally responsible for the full year's tax. If the property changes hands afterward, both the January 1 owner and the new owner receive a bill, and the commissioner does not decide how they divide it. The buyer and seller agree on that, usually at closing.

If a bill goes unpaid, the lien is written in the name of the January 1 owner. The seller can have it issued against the buyer instead by showing, within 90 days of the due date, proof that liability moved. Closing language in which the seller assigns liability for the property taxes to the purchaser and the purchaser accepts it, together with a recorded deed in the purchaser's name, counts as acceptable proof. A delinquent parcel can ultimately be sold at a tax auction.

faqs.q: When are Gwinnett County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are usually due in October or November, after bills go out in August or September. The county listed November 15, 2025 as its previous due date and left the 2026 date to be determined, so use the date printed on your bill.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Gwinnett County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the Annual Notice of Assessment, which is typically mailed in May or June. File with the Board of Assessors, and the county says you can do so online at Gwinnett-Assessor.com.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax if my Gwinnett County house sells after January 1?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is liable for the full year, and both owners may receive a bill. The buyer and seller decide how to split it, and the usual place for that is the closing statement.

faqs.q: What is the Gwinnett Value Offset Exemption?
faqs.a: It is a local exemption that freezes a property's assessed value at its base-year value for the county government portion of your bill. It does not apply to school or city taxes, it covers the home and up to five acres, and it is applied automatically when a homestead exemption is granted.

faqs.q: Can I pay Gwinnett County property tax with cash?
faqs.a: Yes, but only in person at a tax commissioner office. Online payment by check is free, and cards carry a convenience fee. Do not mail cash to the Lawrenceville post office box.
